head: A trucking firm bet
on one small box.
slides.sub: How Yamato built a business no one thought could pay.

image.label: A single cardboard parcel on a Japanese doorstep
image.brief: 1970년대 일본 주택가 현관 앞에 놓인 끈으로 묶은 작은 소포 하나. 아침 햇살, 차분하고 따뜻한 영화 같은 톤. 실제 로고나 마스코트 없음.

head: An old trucking firm,
losing ground.
body: In the early 1970s, Yamato Transport hauled freight for companies. Rivals were winning the long-distance routes, and the 1973 oil shock pushed fuel costs up.
Its president, Masao Ogura, needed a new business, not a cheaper version of the old one.

image.label: Old freight trucks parked in a gray depot
image.brief: 1970년대 일본 화물 터미널에 서 있는 낡은 대형 트럭들. 흐린 하늘, 무거운 분위기. 실제 회사 로고 없음.

head: Sending a parcel
was a chore.
body: If a family wanted to send a box, they wrapped it, tied it with rope and carried it to the post office. Nobody could say when it would arrive.
Ogura saw a need. His directors saw a trap: small, scattered parcels from homes looked impossible to deliver at a profit.

image.label: A woman carrying a rope-tied box to a post office
image.brief: 1970년대 일본 거리에서 끈으로 묶은 상자를 들고 우체국으로 걷는 여성의 뒷모습. 일반적인 인물, 얼굴은 보이지 않게.

head: Your core business is slipping.
What do you do?
body: You run a mid-sized trucking company. Corporate freight is shrinking, and your board fears household parcels will lose money.

options.text: Cut rates to win back big corporate clients
options.feedback: It keeps trucks moving, but you compete on price against stronger rivals. Keep swiping.

options.text: Go all in on household parcels, even if old clients leave
options.feedback: A huge bet with years of thin volume ahead. Keep swiping.

options.text: Add parcels as a side service, keep freight as the core
options.feedback: Lower risk, but half a network rarely gets dense enough to pay. Keep swiping.

image.label: A boardroom table with a small parcel at its center
image.brief: 1970년대 일본 회의실 탁자 한가운데 놓인 작은 소포. 양복 입은 실루엣들이 둘러앉은 구도, 얼굴 없음.

head: Make it easy,
then make it dense.
body: In January 1976, Yamato launched TA-Q-BIN in the Tokyo area. Neighborhood rice and liquor shops took parcels, so no one had to travel far. Prices were simple, set by size and region, and many deliveries arrived the next day.
Ogura believed profit would come once trucks stopped at many homes on each street.

image.label: A small neighborhood shop with parcels stacked by the counter
image.brief: 1970년대 일본 동네 쌀가게 계산대 옆에 쌓인 소포들. 따뜻한 조명, 손글씨 간판. 실제 상표 없음.

slides.label: parcels on the first day, in a story often told
body: Demand built quickly once people learned the service existed. In the first year, Yamato handled about 1.7 million parcels, according to the company.

image.label: An almost empty delivery truck with a few boxes
image.brief: 짐칸에 상자 몇 개만 실린 소형 배달 트럭 내부. 텅 빈 공간이 강조되는 구도.

head: Service first.
Profit later.
body: That was Ogura's rule. Yamato walked away from some of its biggest corporate customers to focus on homes.
It also fought the Ministry of Transport for licenses to run new routes, and in 1986 sued the ministry over delays.

image.label: A delivery driver on a narrow residential street
image.brief: 1980년대 일본 좁은 주택가 골목을 걷는 배달원의 뒷모습. 손에 소포, 일반적인 유니폼, 로고 없음.

head: The network became
the product.
body: As volume grew, each truck covered more homes per street, and costs per parcel fell. Yamato added new services on the same network: ski bags in 1983, golf bags in 1984, chilled food in 1987.
Rivals rushed to copy the model. Home parcels became a new industry in Japan.

image.label: Ski bags and chilled boxes waiting at a depot
image.brief: 1980년대 일본 배송 터미널에 놓인 스키 가방, 골프 가방, 냉장 상자. 활기찬 분위기, 로고 없음.

head: Density turns a loss
into a moat.
body: A route with few stops loses money. The same route with many stops makes it. Yamato fixed the customer's pains first, knowing volume would bring the density that pays.
Just as important, it chose what not to do, leaving freight behind so the whole company served one goal.

image.label: A city map with delivery dots growing denser
image.brief: 도시 지도 위에 배송 지점 점들이 점점 촘촘해지는 그래픽. 어두운 배경, 밝은 점.

head: Some businesses lose money
until they get dense.
body: If your costs fall with volume, the real question is whether you can commit long enough to reach it.
**Try it today:** what would your business look like with twice the customers in the same area, and what would you stop doing to get there?

image.label: Delivery trucks leaving a depot at dawn
image.brief: 새벽에 터미널을 떠나는 소형 배달 트럭들의 행렬. 푸른 새벽빛, 로고 없음.

factChecks.note: 宅急便のサービス開始日(1976年1月20日、関東地区)と小倉昌男の社長就任(1971年)はヤマト運輸の公式社史で確認してください。 → [2026-11-02 확인] 1976년 1월 20일 발매 확인.
「初日の取扱数11個」はヤマト運輸の社史や小倉昌男の著書でよく語られる数字です。カードでは「a story often told」と表示しました。 → [2026-11-02 확인] 첫날 11개는 이번 검색에서 미확인.
初年度の取扱数「約170万個」は会社資料の数字です。カードでは「about」と「according to the company」を付けました。年度区分(1976年度)を確認してください。 → [2026-11-02 확인] 첫해 170만 개 확인.
取締役会の反対、米または酒の販売店を取次店に使った点、「サービスが先、利益は後」の考え方は小倉昌男『小倉昌男 経営学』(1999)に出てきます。直接引用はせず言い換えました。
大口企業貨物からの撤退(1979年前後、三越・松下電器との取引終了とされる)は社名を出さず「some of its biggest corporate customers」とだけ書きました。社史で時期を確認してください。
運輸省に対する行政訴訟(1986年、路線免許の不作為)は当時の報道と著書で確認してください。 → [2026-11-02 확인] 1986년 운수성 부작위 소송 보도 확인(단일 출처).
スキー宅急便(1983年)、ゴルフ宅急便(1984年)、クール宅急便(1988年)の開始年は公式社史基準です。 → [2026-11-02 확인] 스키 1983년·골프 1984년 확인. 쿨 택급편은 1987년이라 1988년을 1987년으로 수정.
